question.text: Grameen Urja Pvt Ltd, an FPE supplying off-grid solar lamps to tribal villages in Jharkhand, has 3-year average revenue of Rs. 12 crore. Mr. Arjun Desai, SIA, must verify that at least 67% is derived from the target population. What is the MINIMUM revenue (any of the three tests) that must flow from eligible activities to the target population?

explanation.text: The Logic: A Social Enterprise must have at least 67% of its activities qualifying as eligible activities targeted at the underserved population. The test can be satisfied through any one of three limbs — Revenue, Expenditure, or Customer base. 67% of Rs. 12 crore = Rs. 8.04 crore. The Trap: 50% is a simple majority and not the SSE threshold. 85% is the Section 11 income-application threshold under the Income Tax Act for charitable trusts — not the SSE primacy test. 100% is unrealistic and not required. Note: When choosing which of the three limbs to attest, pick the one with the strongest documentary support (typically Expenditure, traceable to vouchers and bank statements) and record the choice in the working papers.
